Rob has been running professional mountain courses since 2002 and holds the highest instructional qualification in the UK.
description.shortNote: Drafted from verified website content. Needs editorial tone review.
description.full:
Expedition Guide, run by Rob Johnson WMCI & IML, offers expert mountaineering instruction and guiding from a base in Corris, Southern Snowdonia. Rob has spent more than 20 years guiding clients in the mountains of Britain and further afield — in the European Alps, Norway, Nepal, and Peru — and holds the Winter Mountaineering and Climbing Instructor (WMCI) qualification, the highest instructional award in the UK.

Courses are run throughout the year in Snowdonia and Scotland and cover a wide range of skills. Beginners can start with the two-day Introduction to Scrambling course, tackling iconic Grade 1 routes such as Tryfan's North Ridge and Y Gribin on the Glyderau at a 1:4 instructor-to-student ratio. More experienced hillwalkers can progress to the Advanced Scrambling (Learn to Lead) course, which introduces roped techniques on Grade 2 and 3 scrambles. The six-day MountainCraft course covers the full Mountain Leader syllabus — navigation, steep ground, wild camping, and night navigation — and is the recommended starting point for those pursuing the Mountain Leader qualification.

Rob is an approved Mountain Training Cymru provider and course director (provider number 1554) for Mountain Leader training and assessment. He is a full member of the Association of Mountaineering Instructors (AMI), the British Association of International Mountain Leaders (BAIML), and the Mountain Training Association (MTA). Courses are assisted by Huw Gilbert, who also holds the WMCI qualification.
